name: Passalacqua
tagline: Twenty-four rooms in an 18th-century villa on Lake Como, with seven acres of garden.
description:
Passalacqua is a 24-room hotel in an 18th-century villa at Moltrasio on Lake Como, about fifteen minutes from the town of Como and an hour's drive from Milan. It opened in June 2022 after a three-year restoration.

Count Andrea Lucini-Passalacqua had the villa built in 1787, to a design by the Milanese architect Carlo Felice Soave. The composer Vincenzo Bellini wrote La Sonnambula during a stay in 1831, and Winston Churchill was among later visitors. The De Santis family, who own the Grand Hotel Tremezzo, bought the house in 2018. Seven acres of gardens fall away to a private jetty, and the hotel, restaurant and gardens are open only to guests. The hotel closes from early January to early March.

The rooms are divided between three buildings. The Villa has twelve, from 40 square metre rooms to the Suite Bellini, which measures 250 square metres and looks over the lake. The Palazz, behind the Villa, has eight rooms averaging 37 square metres, and the Casa al Lago, close to the water in the garden, has four, which can be taken together for exclusive use. Suite Norma and Suite Agnese, in the Villa, measure 120 and 90 square metres.

Chef Viviana Varese runs the kitchen. Dinner is served on the candlelit terrace or in the Sala Ovale, under frescoed ceilings, and breakfast is a buffet in the kitchen with an island for eggs. The pool bar, the Winter Garden, is a former greenhouse designed by JJ Martin of La DoubleJ, and aperitivo is taken in the bar, by the pool or on the terrace.

The spa is in the Palazz and uses Seed to Skin, a Tuscan skincare line. Below the gardens, an 18th-century gallery holds a sauna, a steam bath and a heated indoor pool that can be reserved for one party. The lake-view pool sits on a terrace below the villa. A clay tennis court, bocce, a gym in a former greenhouse and open-air cinema evenings fill the days, and a seasonal programme of activities, such as a tour of the underground tunnels and a gelato class, is included in every stay. Boats leave from the jetty, among them the vintage launch Giumello II and a restored Riva Olympic.

The hotel suits guests who want a villa on the lake with a small number of rooms, a kitchen that works with the seasons and the town of Como close by.
